title: How Roboflow Helps with Compliance and Readiness for Computer Vision
summary: Clear security, legal, and labor reviews faster. Blur faces, govern AI agents, scope API keys, and run AI on-prem or air-gapped with Roboflow.
body_markdown:
SUMMARY


**Roboflow helps teams meet compliance requirements and get computer vision ready for security, legal, and operations review, with documented controls: blur and pixelate blocks you can run on your own hardware to anonymize people before images leave your site, agents that ask before they act, scoped and rotatable API keys, custom roles and audit logs, and self-hosted Inference that can run fully offline. Start any review at the**[Roboflow Trust Center (opens in a new tab)](https://security.roboflow.com/?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**


Computer vision projects rarely stall because a model is not accurate enough. They stall in compliance and readiness review. Security teams want to know where data lives and who can touch it. Legal teams ask about faces, consent, and biometric laws. Plant managers and labor relations teams want to know how cameras on the floor will land with the people who work there. And now that AI agents and large language models are part of the toolkit, IT teams want to know exactly what those systems can do.


In this guide, we'll show how Roboflow helps you meet compliance requirements across biometrics, agent readiness, union rules and worker monitoring, using OpenAI models safely, custom governance, API keys, and local deployment. For each one, we cover what Roboflow documents today and link to the source.


## Compliance and Readiness for Computer Vision with Roboflow


Below are seven areas reviewers ask about most, with the features and design patterns that address each one in Roboflow.


### 1. How Roboflow Handles Biometric Data and Face Privacy


Roboflow Workflows include built-in blocks for anonymizing people and faces:


- [Blur Visualization (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks/visualize-predictions/blur-visualization?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **:** Blurs detected regions, and follows the exact mask shape when a segmentation model is available. A padding setting grows each region so edges the model missed, such as hair and hands, are still covered. Its documented use cases include blurring faces, people, and license plates to anonymize content before sharing or publishing.
- [Pixelate Visualization (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks/visualize-predictions/pixelate-visualization?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **:** Pixelates detected regions. It can feed storage blocks such as Roboflow Dataset Upload, so the image that gets saved is the anonymized one.
- [Image Blur (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks/classical-computer-vision/image-blur?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **:** Applies a classical blur to a whole image.


**People blurred inside their detected bounding boxes, from**[our tutorial](https://roboflow.com/blog/how-to-blur-a-bounding-box-python?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **on blurring a bounding box in Python.**


Pair a face or person detector with one of these blocks, run it on your own hardware, and the raw frame never needs to leave your site. For step by step guides, see[face blurring for privacy](https://roboflow.com/blog/face-blur-privacy-computer-vision?ref=blog.roboflow.com) ,[blurring people with an API](https://roboflow.com/blog/blur-people-api?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , and[how to blur a bounding box in Python](https://roboflow.com/blog/how-to-blur-a-bounding-box-python?ref=blog.roboflow.com) .


### 2. Agent Readiness: How to Govern AI Agents in Roboflow


AI agents can now build datasets, train models, and assemble Workflows. That is a big productivity gain, and it raises a fair question from security teams: what exactly can an agent do, and how do we govern it?


Roboflow offers[four agent surfaces (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/agents/agents?ref=blog.roboflow.com) : an MCP server, open source[Agent Skills (opens in a new tab)](https://github.com/roboflow/computer-vision-skills?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , OpenAPI specs, and the in-app Roboflow Agent. Each one is built with control in mind.


- **Scoped sign in for MCP clients.** The[Roboflow MCP server (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/agents/mcp-server?ref=blog.roboflow.com) uses OAuth, with a consent page that shows which Roboflow account is connecting. The docs cover Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT and Codex, and our[MCP page](https://roboflow.com/mcp?ref=blog.roboflow.com) adds setup for Gemini CLI. Each tool declares the OAuth scopes it needs, and your client only gets the scopes you approve at sign in. Clients receive a scoped access token tied to your workspace.
- **The Agent asks before it acts.** The[Roboflow Agent (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/agents/roboflow-agent?ref=blog.roboflow.com) asks before it starts a Workflow Evals run that costs credits, and saves the best Workflow from an Eval as an unpublished draft. Before it copies a Universe dataset, you agree on sources, image counts, and class changes in chat. A Workflow the agent creates through the Agent API is live right away, so set production Workflows to Protected: agent edits then stay drafts until you publish them. Learn more about[how Agent keeps your data inside the lines](https://roboflow.com/blog/how-roboflow-agent-keeps-your-data-inside-the-lines?ref=blog.roboflow.com) .
- **Edge devices are read only.** The Agent has read only access to your Deployment Manager fleet, telemetry, logs, and streams.
- **Bring your own model key.** With Workspace LLM Keys, the Agent, the Workflow editor assistant, the custom block assistant, and the Agent API can run on your own OpenAI or Azure OpenAI key, so your data does not go through Roboflow's LLM keys.
- **Agents follow your existing controls.** Agents work inside the same controls you use for people:[audit logs (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/platform/enterprise-features/audit-logs-and-siem-export?ref=blog.roboflow.com) that record actions by a user, API key, or system,[custom roles (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/platform/enterprise-features/role-based-access-control?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , scoped API keys (see section 6), and Workflows Block Governance (see section 5). A scoped key with folder restrictions limits the Agent API to Workflows and models in that folder, and a protected key cannot be taken down by an agent or script that has key management scopes.


### Enforce Your Own Model Key


When you turn on[Enforce Workspace LLM Keys (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/changelog/changelog/october-2026/workspace-llm-keys-enforce-your-own-openai-key?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , every request uses your key and never falls back to Roboflow's. Features that cannot use your key are turned off, image generation is turned off, and conversation traces are not recorded.


### 3. Design Patterns for Union Rules and Worker Monitoring


Cameras on a production floor can raise real concerns for the people who work there, and many sites operate under collective bargaining agreements or wo\`rks council rules. What we offer are design patterns that keep a system focused on processes, not people:


- **Anonymize people by default.** Use the Blur or Pixelate Visualization blocks on your own hardware to obscure people in every frame before footage leaves your site or is shared. Our guide to[blurring people](https://roboflow.com/blog/blur-people-api?ref=blog.roboflow.com) covers the common case where people are incidental to a computer vision deployment, and our[advanced Workflows tutorial](https://roboflow.com/blog/how-to-create-advanced-workflows?ref=blog.roboflow.com) builds a privacy first pipeline where anonymization is the default and anyone outside a restricted zone is pixelated.
- **Keep footage on site.** Run models on your own servers or edge devices so video stays inside your facility network.
- **Limit who can see what, and keep a record.** Use custom roles and project folder permissions so only the right people can view footage or results, and use audit logs to keep a tamper-resistant, reviewable record of changes such as role updates, folder access changes, and exports.
- **Measure processes, not individuals.** Design use cases around equipment, materials, zones, and safety conditions, such as whether a guard is in place or a walkway is clear, rather than the performance of named individuals. Store counts and events instead of identities wherever you can.


**Part of a Workflow from our**[advanced Workflows tutorial](https://roboflow.com/blog/how-to-create-advanced-workflows?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **, with tracking, detection filters, time in zone, and a Pixelate Visualization block in the visualization chain.**


### How to Redact On Site, Then Send Images to OpenAI


Large multimodal models such as OpenAI's GPT models are useful for describing scenes, reading text, and answering open ended questions about images. Many teams want those capabilities without sending raw images that contain faces or other sensitive details to a third party model provider. The answer is to redact first, on hardware you control, and send only the anonymized image.


OpenAI models are available as a Workflows block. You can call them with a[Roboflow managed key billed in credits (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/changelog/changelog/june-2025/use-a-managed-openai-api-key-in-workflows?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , or with your own key. If a workspace must never send images to an outside model, admins can use[Workflows Block Governance (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks-governance?ref=blog.roboflow.com) to disable the OpenAI block and other blocks that call external AI providers, and those changes are recorded in audit logs.


Every piece of the setup below is documented.


**Step 1: Run Inference on Your Own Hardware**


Install[self-hosted Inference (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/deployment/self-hosted/self-hosted?ref=blog.roboflow.com) on a server or edge device you control. Self-hosted Inference runs Workflows locally, so the redaction step happens before any image leaves your network.


**Step 2: Build the Redaction Workflow**


Create a new Workflow and add these blocks in order:


Block


Role


Image input


The raw camera frame. It stays on your hardware.


Detection or segmentation model


Finds faces, people, license plates, or other sensitive regions.


Blur Visualization or Pixelate Visualization


Anonymizes each detected region. With a segmentation model, Blur follows the exact mask shape.


OpenAI block


Receives only the anonymized image, plus your prompt.


Connect the image and the model's detections to the Blur or Pixelate block, then connect the anonymized image from that block to the OpenAI block. Only the anonymized image is passed on.


**An OpenAI block inside a Roboflow Workflow, from our guide to using**[OpenAI for computer vision](https://roboflow.com/blog/openai-computer-vision?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**


**Step 3: Choose Which Key Pays for the Request**


Pick a Roboflow managed key or your own. With Workspace LLM Keys enforced, the Workflow OpenAI and Gemini blocks and Auto Label run their OpenAI and Gemini models on your own OpenAI or Gemini key, with no fallback to Roboflow's keys, and other LLM blocks that cannot use your keys are turned off. Auto Label can also[run on your own OpenAI or Gemini key (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/changelog/changelog/september-2026/auto-label-run-with-your-openai-or-gemini-key?ref=blog.roboflow.com) .


As noted in section 2, enforcement is enabled per workspace and is not available in the EU region today. When you[share a Workflow (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/manage/share-a-workflow?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , by default it does not run under your keys, and credentials such as an OpenAI key become inputs the other person provides. If you choose to let others run it with your hidden credentials, those credentials are redacted from any client facing data.


### 4. Test Before You Connect a Live Camera


Run a set of test images through the Workflow and review the output before you point it at a live feed. Include hard cases: faces at an angle, partly hidden, or far from the camera. To keep an anonymized copy for training, connect the Pixelate Visualization output to the Roboflow Dataset Upload block. The image that gets saved is the anonymized one.


### 5. Custom Governance for Large Organizations


Large organizations rarely have one set of rules. Different business units, sites, and data types need different controls. Roboflow Enterprise includes tools to shape governance to your organization:


- **Custom roles:**[Custom role based access control (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/platform/enterprise-features/role-based-access-control?ref=blog.roboflow.com) lets you define roles with exactly the permissions each team needs.
- **Folder level permissions:**[Project folder permissions (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/datasets/manage/project-folders/project-folder-permissions?ref=blog.roboflow.com) let you organize work by business unit, site, or sensitivity level and control who can access each folder. With[single sign on (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/platform/enterprise-features/single-sign-on-sso?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , folder permissions can follow your identity provider groups, including Active Directory group sync.
- [Workflows Block Governance (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks-governance?ref=blog.roboflow.com) : Choose which Workflow blocks are available in each workspace, including blocks that call external AI providers, so a block that does not meet your security, privacy, or compliance requirements cannot be added to Workflows. Block changes are recorded in audit logs.
- **Audit logs with SIEM export:**[Audit logs (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/platform/enterprise-features/audit-logs-and-siem-export?ref=blog.roboflow.com) record actions by users, API keys, and systems, covering events such as API key changes, OAuth apps, and exports. Logs are tamper-resistant, queryable for 365 days by default, and can stream to your SIEM over OpenTelemetry.
- **Private by default:** On Enterprise plans, public projects are off by default and the setting can be locked by your plan, a compliance policy, or the EU region.


### 6. How to Scope, Rotate, and Secure API Keys


API keys are often the most direct path to your data and models, so they deserve the same care as any other credential. Our[key management docs (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/authentication/authentication/manage-api-keys-in-the-dashboard?ref=blog.roboflow.com) describe how every workspace can create, name, roll, protect, and revoke API keys. Viewing, creating, updating, revoking, and using keys are separate permissions, so you decide who can do what.


Protected keys cannot be disabled, revoked, or rolled, so protect production keys and an automated agent or script with key management scopes cannot take them down. Only the dashboard can unprotect a key.


Before you roll, revoke, or disable a key, a dependency warning shows what relies on it: Dedicated Deployments, billing folders, edge devices, whether it is the workspace default key, and its billed usage over the last 30 days.


[Advanced API Keys (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/authentication/authentication/scoped-api-keys?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , an Enterprise add-on, adds scoped permissions, folder keys, custom metadata, disabling, a default key, and rotation reminders. Here is how to use them to set up keys for a new site.


**Step 1: Create a Folder Key for the Site**


Folder keys reach only one project folder. The docs recommend one key per site, production line, or integration, so a rotation or a leak affects only one folder.


**The API Keys dialog for one project folder, with full access and scoped keys, rotation dates, disabled keys, and owners recorded in key metadata.**[Source (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/authentication/authentication/scoped-api-keys?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**


**Step 2: Limit the Key to the Scopes It Needs**


A new scoped key gets every ability except managing API keys, so it cannot read or manage other keys unless you opt in. Remove anything the integration does not use. A request outside a key's scopes gets a 404, as if the route did not exist. You can also scope a key to a role with role:<name>.


**Generating a new key with custom metadata, a rotation due date, owners, and key permissions.**[Source (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/authentication/authentication/scoped-api-keys?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**


**Step 3: Label the Key with an Owner**


Add custom metadata, up to 20 key and value pairs, such as owner and env. When it is time to rotate, you know who to call.


**Step 4: Plan the Rotation**


Our[rotation guidance (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/authentication/authentication/rotate-api-keys?ref=blog.roboflow.com) recommends rotating about once a year. This is a guideline, not a requirement, so keys keep working past the date and your own policy decides. Rotate immediately if a key is exposed.


- **Roll, don't rebuild.** Rolling a key revokes and replaces it in one step, keeps its name, permissions, folders, and metadata, and moves Dedicated Deployments automatically.
- **Keep two people on every key.** Make sure at least two people can rotate each key.
- **Use reminders.** With Advanced API Keys, owners get one reminder email between 15 days before a key's rotation due date and the date itself.


**Settings, API Keys, with workspace keys, their rotation badges, and row actions.**[Source (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/authentication/authentication/manage-api-keys-in-the-dashboard?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**


### 7. Run Computer Vision On-Prem, at the Edge, or Air-Gapped


For many industrial and regulated environments, the strongest privacy control is simple: keep the data where it is created. Roboflow Inference is open source and runs on hardware you control. As our[deployment guide (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/deployment/choosing-a-deployment?ref=blog.roboflow.com) puts it, "If your workload must stay on-prem, on the edge, or air-gapped, run Self-Hosted Inference."


**Choose a Deployment Model**


Option


What it does


Where data stays


Self-hosted Inference


Runs models and Workflows on servers or edge devices you control.


On your hardware.


[Offline Mode (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/deployment/self-hosted/enterprise/offline-mode?ref=blog.roboflow.com) (Enterprise)


Caches model weights for up to 30 days in a Docker container.


Completely air-gapped.


[Secure Gateway (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/deployment/self-hosted/enterprise/secure-gateway?ref=blog.roboflow.com) (Enterprise)


Proxies the routes deployment servers need into your DMZ and caches weights and container images locally.


Behind one controlled point of egress for the whole fleet.


**Deployment options compared, from the Serverless Cloud API to air-gapped Offline Mode, showing where images stay in each.**[Source](https://roboflow.com/blog/model-weight-security?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**


Offline Workflow execution is also an Enterprise feature. In the strictest setup described in our[air-gapped deployment guide](https://roboflow.com/blog/air-gapped-computer-vision-deployment?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , the camera feed, weights, results, and records all stay inside the plant network. Secure Gateway runs on Docker, Kubernetes, RHEL with Podman, or MicroShift, and has an air-gapped bundle. It replaces the deprecated License Server.


**Three network isolation patterns from our air-gapped deployment guide: fully air-gapped, an isolated plant network, and restricted egress through Secure Gateway in a DMZ.**[Source](https://roboflow.com/blog/air-gapped-computer-vision-deployment?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**


**Tip:** For air-gapped deployments, the docs recommend pinning versions.


### Manage It at Scale


[Enterprise deployment features (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/deployment/self-hosted/enterprise?ref=blog.roboflow.com) include Deployment Manager for remote fleets, Secure Gateway, offline mode, Kubernetes, and Docker Compose, along with a commercial license to self-host certain open model families, including offline deployment. Learn more in our posts on[on-premise computer vision](https://roboflow.com/blog/on-premise-computer-vision?ref=blog.roboflow.com) ,[deploying models offline](https://roboflow.com/blog/deploy-computer-vision-models-offline?ref=blog.roboflow.com) ,[data diodes for computer vision](https://roboflow.com/blog/data-diode-computer-vision?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , and[managing computer vision across an edge fleet](https://roboflow.com/blog/managing-computer-vision-across-an-edge-fleet?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , or visit our[air-gapped AI deployment page](https://roboflow.com/ai/air-gapped-ai-deployment?ref=blog.roboflow.com) .


**Deployment Manager sends Workflow settings to local Inference, the camera feeds the Workflow on site, and selected records go to Vision Events.**[Source](https://roboflow.com/blog/managing-computer-vision-across-an-edge-fleet?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **.**
